subject.title: [Feature]: Support for Custom Emojis in Latest Telegram Bot API Update

question: What public representation should OpenClaw support for outgoing Telegram custom emoji: raw `<tg-emoji>` HTML only, typed Telegram `entities` / `caption_entities` on the message tool, or a shared Markdown/IR custom-emoji span?
rationale: Current code partially supports raw HTML tags, but the remaining gap changes the shared message-tool/plugin API and Telegram send-funnel semantics, so automation should not pick the permanent public contract.

options.title: Add Typed Entity Contract
options.body: Define a validated entity representation for the message tool and Telegram plugin, forward it through send/edit/caption/reply paths, and keep current HTML/plain fallback behavior for ordinary sends.

options.title: Treat Raw HTML as Sufficient
options.body: Document the existing `<tg-emoji>` passthrough as the supported path and close or narrow the remaining entity-array work to cases with concrete product approval.

options.title: Fold Into Formatting Policy
options.body: Defer implementation until the broader Telegram parse-mode/rich-message policy in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/10944 decides how raw HTML, MarkdownV2, rich messages, and entities should coexist.

recommendation.title: Add Typed Entity Contract
recommendation.body: Define a validated entity representation for the message tool and Telegram plugin, forward it through send/edit/caption/reply paths, and keep current HTML/plain fallback behavior for ordinary sends.
